text:
For about a year I had a constant feeling of emptiness, as if I really was hollow inside. I'd go through the motions of life, eat, sleep, look for jobs, but it felt like an empty body doing things. The depression I'd had before got much worse. I had thoughts of suicide, though I never made a plan. I felt like I'd made myself worse by trying to fix myself.

I had episodes of depersonalisation where I'd feel like I was going back into the void, usually at night. Lying on the kitchen floor was a flashback I had many times. I avoided my kitchen for a while, which is not easy in a small apartment.

Strangely, once the lockdown ended and I could see people again, it slowly got better. I think a lot of it was the isolation.
Ich habe seitdem große Angst vor dem Meer und vor Booten. Ich kann nicht mehr segeln. Wenn ich Sturm höre, bekomme ich Herzrasen. Ich hatte auch einige Monate lang Albträume, in denen ich ertrinke.
A bit of health anxiety for a while, nothing major.

The aftermath has been long and complex.

For the first few weeks, I had profound derealisation. My home, my wife, my colleagues, all felt like a stage set that could be dismantled at any moment. I kept expecting the 'real' world, the DMT world, to break through. I couldn't fully believe in ordinary reality.

Then came existential terror. The belief that my human life is a brief dream and that there's an infinite realm waiting for me where I'm nobody was hard to shake. I had panic attacks at night where I felt I was slipping back into that place. I was afraid to sleep, because sleep felt like a doorway.

I became depressed. My work, which I'd always found meaningful, felt trivial. Why study anything if this is all a dream? I took two months of leave.

Over time, I came to see the experience differently. I now think my mind created an extremely convincing world, and the terror came from the loss of self, not from any truth about reality. That helped. I also gained a deep appreciation for being embodied and ordinary, for my wife's face, for coffee in the morning. But it took more than a year to get there.

The hip took months to heal and I had to use a walker. I felt foolish and ashamed. My fear of death got worse, not better, the opposite of what I'd hoped. I also had nightmares about falling. My wife was very upset with me and with the guide. I felt depressed for some months.

I developed strong social anxiety. I couldn't go to lectures because I felt everyone was looking at me and thinking of the video. I stopped eating in the dining hall. I'd hear people laughing and immediately think they were laughing at me. I had panic attacks when I saw my old roommate.

I became depressed. I felt worthless and stupid. I stopped talking to my parents because I didn't want them to find out. I failed most of my classes that semester and nearly dropped out.

I also had flashbacks of the bathroom mirror and my face distorting. For a long time I couldn't look at myself in a mirror without feeling sick.

I still struggle to trust people, especially in groups. I'm very careful about who I'm vulnerable with.

After that ceremony the memories of the abuse came back more vividly than ever before. I had been in therapy for years and thought I had processed it. Now I was having flashbacks again, sometimes several a day. Triggers I'd overcome came back: certain aftershaves, the sound of a belt buckle, men of his age with a particular build.

I had nightmares almost every night, often of the ceremony circle with him in it. I started sleeping with a light on. I had trouble being touched, even by my partner. I also had periods of dissociation where I'd lose time.

I felt deeply betrayed, by the medicine, by myself, by the people who had promised it would heal me. I had believed that ayahuasca would be the final step in my healing and instead it set me back years. I became very depressed. I had to take time off work. I had suicidal thoughts that I hadn't had since my early twenties.

My anxiety was constant, a feeling of being watched. I checked locks and windows obsessively.

It's been two years. Some of it has eased. But I'm not back to where I was before the ceremony.

Seit dem Retreat habe ich immer wieder Flashbacks an die Nacht, vor allem an das Gesicht des Mannes unter der Decke. Diese Bilder kommen oft ohne Vorwarnung, beim Einschlafen, beim Duschen, manchmal mitten im Gespräch. Ich habe fast jede Nacht Albträume, in denen ich in der Hütte liege und nicht weg kann, während jemand stirbt.

Ich habe eine starke Angst vor dem Tod entwickelt, meine eigene und die meiner Familie. Ich habe ständig Angst, dass jemandem etwas passiert. Wenn mein Mann sich nicht sofort meldet, bekomme ich Panik.

Ich hatte auch Schuldgefühle, weil ich nichts getan habe, obwohl ich so nah war. Ich weiß, dass ich nichts hätte tun können, aber das Gefühl bleibt.

In den ersten Monaten war ich wie betäubt, ich habe kaum etwas gefühlt, außer Angst. Dann kam eine Depression. Ich konnte nicht mehr arbeiten und war fast ein Jahr krankgeschrieben.

I had nightmares about Sam's blue face for months, sometimes it was my own face. I couldn't go to raves or clubs anymore. Whenever someone didn't answer their phone I'd panic that they were dead. I had a lot of guilt for not knowing he was taking G and for being too high to help properly. My friends noticed I'd become very anxious and controlling, always checking on everyone.
Ich hatte ein paar Wochen lang das Gefühl, dass ich jederzeit wieder in die Maschine fallen könnte. Danach ist es verschwunden.
